plain_summary: A supply of isoniazid during warfarin treatment calls for a review of the interaction and the patient's INR monitoring.

medicine_groups.name: Warfarin
medicine_groups.note: Use the dated supply and the current anticoagulation directions.

medicine_groups.name: Isoniazid
medicine_groups.note: Count isoniazid as a single ingredient or as part of a tuberculosis regimen. Count combination packs containing isoniazid, including tablets labelled as rifampicin with isoniazid or as Rifinah.

rule_for_models: In a patient taking Group A warfarin, suspect a finding when Group A and Group B (isoniazid) supply dates overlap or fall within 60 days of each other and the intended courses can overlap. Use the form, directions, quantity and any recorded hold or stop to exclude courses that cannot coincide. Cite both supplies even if there is no INR result. When the supplies are within 60 days and unclear directions leave overlap uncertain, cite both supplies and report only a possible finding. Ask the pharmacist to confirm the dose actually used and the treatment dates. A documented stop, hold or later start that rules out overlap gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: The supplies alone cannot show whether both medicines were taken, how the INR changed, whether bleeding occurred or what monitoring was arranged elsewhere.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the full tuberculosis regimen, including any rifampicin, alongside recent INR results and the monitoring plan?
